rows.question: Can you read https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crappie and tell me the scientific genus of crappie?
rows.answer: [smiling] Sure thing! According to Wikipedia, crappie belong to the genus *Pomoxis*. The name comes from Greek words meaning "sharp cover," which refers to their spiny gill covers. There are two species: black crappie (*Pomoxis nigromaculatus*) and white crappie (*Pomoxis annularis*).

rows.question: Look at https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html and tell me which function turns a Python object into a JSON string.
rows.answer: [smiling] The function that turns a Python object into a JSON string is `json.dumps()`. I found this on the Python 3.15.2 documentation site (docs.python.org). It takes a Python data structure and returns its JSON string representation.

rows.question: Research this for me: start at https://docs.python.org/3/library/index.html and follow the links to find what the json module's dumps function does.
rows.answer: [attentive] Sure, let me follow that link to the json module page. I found it! From Python's official documentation (python.org), the json.dumps function converts a Python object into a JSON-formatted string. It takes data like lists, dictionaries, and other objects and turns them into text that follows the JSON standard. You can also customize how it formats the output—like sorting keys alphabetically or adding indentation for readability—and even handle special types like complex numbers with a custom function.

sources.title: json — JSON encoder and decoder — Python 3.15.2 documentation

rows.question: Start at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_education and follow the links to the article about the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act. What year was it first passed?
rows.answer: [smiling] The Individuals with Disabilities Education Act was first passed in 1975 when it was originally called the Education for All Handicapped Children Act. It was renamed IDEA in 1990, according to Wikipedia.

sources.title: Individuals with Disabilities Education Act - Wikipedia

rows.question: Can you look up when Steely Dan was formed?
rows.answer: [smiling] Steely Dan was formed in 1971 by Walter Becker and Donald Fagen in Annandale-on-Hudson, New York. They met while they were students at Bard College and started the band together.

rows.question: Search the web for how tall Mount Rainier is.
rows.answer: [smiling] Mount Rainier stands at 14,406 feet (4,391 meters) tall, according to Wikipedia. It’s the highest mountain in Washington state and one of the most prominent peaks in the contiguous United States.

rows.question: Look up what year Dan Fogelberg released the song Longer.
rows.answer: [smiling] Dan Fogelberg released "Longer" in 1979, specifically on December 8th that year. It came from his album *Phoenix*. I found this information on Wikipedia.

rows.question: Is the internet useful for finding recipes?
rows.answer: [smiling] Yes, the internet is very useful for finding recipes! It offers a vast array of options, from quick weeknight meals to elaborate holiday dishes. Many sites provide step-by-step instructions, ingredient lists, and even nutritional information.
